body:
I am not able to reproduce this behavior with Rails v6.0.0.rc1 as well as on the latest master.

I get the expected error [screenshot].

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/876195/58365474-96d8a580-7ee2-11e9-8e71-3c59d2f541a2.png)

@vishaltelangre you need to not close the string in the name of the template:

```
<%= render 'my_fake_template %>
```

Checked the surrounding source code for `source_extract` and `annotated_source_code` they've been in there for years!

However, this is new https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/35308

Looks like my original report has a typo, I did intend to close the string in my example. It should be:

```
<%= render 'my_fake_template' %>
```

I think I've narrowed this down to multi line ruby templates being the culprit:

In the below example the line number for the error: "missing partial ..." should be attributed correctly to line 1.

```erb
     1	<%= render 'missing_template' %>
     2	<%=
     3		my_helper(
     4			:a,
     5			:b,
     6			:c,
     7			d: {
     8				e: :e,
     9				f: :f,
    10			}
    11		)
    12	%>
    13	
```

However, when the `render` call appears after the multi-line template the error's line number is equal to it's *real* line number plus the length of the range of the multi-line template.

    n_reported = n_real + (n_templateEnd - n_templateStart)

In the below example, the multi-line template spans 11 lines, and the error should occur on line 12; therefore the reported line number of the error will be line 22.

    n_reported = 11 - 1 + 12 = 22

```ruby
     1	<%=
     2		my_helper(
     3			:a,
     4			:b,
     5			:c,
     6			d: {
     7				e: :e,
     8				f: :f,
     9			}
    10		)
    11	%>
    12	<%= render 'missing_template' %>
```

issue.title: Autoload SyntaxErrorInTemplate
issue.body: ### Summary Came out of looking into this: https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/36341 When a SyntaxError is detected in a template we raise this exception: `SyntaxErrorInTemplate`. On a first request to the server the exception we get a NameError since the exception is not required from `active_view/template/error.rb` yet. However later on it gets required and a second request will succeed. On the first request we see the rails "Something Wen Wrong" page and not the expected syntax error in template error page with the webconsole and stacktrace. By autoloading the constant we fix this issue. Before the patch the first request looks like: And the log information is silenced by the `DebugExceptions` middleware. After the patch this looks like: cc: @gmcgibbon

body:
I had a 👀 into this and found a deeper issue going on here. When we find a syntax error in the template, such as a missing `'` in `<%= render 'missing_template' %>`, we wrap the `SyntaxError` into a `SyntaxErrorInTemplate` exception and raise that one: https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/aae270de9e0862f31b14642908472d235a17936f/actionview/lib/action_view/template.rb#L341-L345 The issue here is that the `SyntaxErrorInTemplate` constant hasn't gotten required yet. So this line ends up raising a `NameError: unitialized constant ActionView::Template::SyntaxErrorInTemplate` in actuality. Later on within the debug exceptions middleware we catch this exception and go to render it, at the point of logging the exception as @Dkendal pointed out the `annotated_source_code` method returns `nil` which causes the type error: `TypeError: no implicit conversion of nil into Array` to be raised. What the developer ends up seeing is this page on the first request:
Something Went Wrong Page
Later on the `SyntaxErrorInTemplate` is required by this check that occurs after the attempt to render: https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/aae270de9e0862f31b14642908472d235a17936f/actionview/lib/action_view/template.rb#L349-L350 So on the second request the we see the desired exception page:
Exception View
The reason the `annotated_source_code` method returns nil is because when its extracting the source code it will look for the occurrence of the template file name in the backtrace: https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/aae270de9e0862f31b14642908472d235a17936f/actionview/lib/action_view/template/error.rb#L107-L108 However in this case the exception was a `NameError` that happened before the evaluation of the template and so the template file name won't be in the backtrace and thus the method returns nil. The fix for this is implemented in this PR: https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/36521, this will resolve the issue of the `TypeError: no implicit conversion of nil into array`. It won't however resolve the issue of line numbers however, but that is a separate issue.

issue.title: Empty array instead of nil for source_extract
issue.body:
### Summary

The source_extract method will return nil when it can't find the file name in
the backtrace, methods that consume this method expect an array and the nil ends
up causing type errors down the road like it happened here: #36341. This patch
introduces a to_a call that converts the nil into an empty array this makes it so
client classes can correctly handle a empty list of source code lines and not
trigger a type error.

### Other Information

Note this is a bit defensive and preventative imo, this occured for the edge case described here: https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/36341#issuecomment-503673532 and potentially other unknown code paths could still cause this behaviour to occur, but I don't know of any. 

At any rate I do like having the method return a `[]` instead of a nil and thing that is a better interface for this class in general since the method will be returning consistent types. 

discussed this with @rafaelfranca and @gmcgibbon
